meta.ogImageAlt: IPAForge: install SideStore and your own apps onto iPhone and iPad from Windows, macOS and Linux.

home.title: IPAForge: install SideStore from Windows, macOS and Linux
home.description: IPAForge is a free, open-source desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux that installs SideStore and your own apps onto iPhone and iPad with a free Apple ID.

hero.lede: IPAForge installs SideStore and your own apps onto iPhone and iPad with a free Apple ID, from Windows, macOS or Linux. It checks everything before it changes anything, and when something fails, it tells you how to fix it.

limits.title: Apple's limits, shown before you hit them.
limits.sub: A free Apple ID can sideload, within rules most tools leave you to discover. IPAForge counts them for you and says what an install will use.
limits.apps: at a time on each device. IPAForge asks which one to replace when you reach it.
limits.days: per signature. IPAForge refreshes your apps by itself before they expire.
limits.appIds: shown before installing, with when the next one frees up.

features.title: Everything sideloading needs, in one app.

sidestore.title: One-click SideStore
sidestore.body: SideStore, or LiveContainer with SideStore, Stable or Nightly. The pairing file and certificate are placed for you.

preload.title: Preload your apps
preload.body: Drop .ipa files, paste a link, or browse the catalog, SideStore's source and any AltStore-format source you add.

refresh.title: Apps that don't expire
refresh.body: See when each app expires. Refresh works like SideStore's: a new profile while your certificate is valid, nothing reinstalled.

repair.title: Repair SideStore
repair.body: Checks what keeps SideStore from refreshing by itself, line by line, and fixes it in one go.

qr.title: QR codes for SideStore
qr.body: Add a source to SideStore on your iPhone, or have SideStore install an app, by scanning a code.

checklist.title: A checklist for each iPhone
checklist.body: Trust, passcode, Developer Mode, trusting your Apple ID, LocalDevVPN: what your iOS version needs, ticked as you go.

recovery.title: Recovery, not dead ends
recovery.body: Every failure has a screen with the fixes that apply, copyable diagnostics and a pre-filled bug report.

progress.title: Live progress
progress.body: Every step shows what it's doing: speed and time left while sending the app, Apple's steps, and iOS's own install progress, over USB or Wi-Fi.

logs.title: Logs you can share
logs.body: Every step IPAForge took, with search and filters, saved to a file to attach to a bug report.

accounts.title: Several Apple IDs
accounts.body: Two-factor sign-in with a code on your devices or by text. Kept in your system keychain, free and paid teams, with a quick switch when Apple blocks one on a device.

anisette.title: Anisette servers your way
anisette.body: IPAForge picks a working server from SideStore's list by itself, with a backup. Or choose one, add your own, and test each.

updates.title: Updates itself
updates.body: A new version installs when IPAForge opens, after its release signature checks out, and What's new tells you what changed.

languages.title: Your language, your look
languages.body: {count} languages, right to left included, and six colour themes in light and dark.

plug.title: Plug in your iPhone
plug.body: Unlock it and tap Trust. The checklist shows what else your iOS version needs, like Developer Mode.

signIn.title: Sign in with your Apple ID
signIn.body: A free account works. Your password goes only to Apple, and saved Apple IDs stay in your system keychain.

install.title: Install
install.body: IPAForge signs SideStore, places its pairing file and certificate, and installs it, showing every step as it goes.

open.title: You can read every line, and check every download.
open.typescript: All TypeScript, no closed helpers. Code signing, talking to the device and signing in to Apple are written from scratch and open to read.
open.signs: Signs like Apple. The signer's output matches Apple's own codesign byte for byte on its test fixtures, and Apple's verifier accepts it.
open.signed: Signed releases. Every file of every release carries a Sigstore signature from the release workflow, and IPAForge checks it before installing an update.
open.license: AGPL-3.0, and it stays open. Free to use, study, change and share, and anything built from it must stay open source too.
open.appLogs: # what the app logs before an update installs

engine.title: The engine and the app
engine.body: Signer, device layer, Apple sign-in, developer services, the installer and the interface.

guide.title: Guided first run
guide.body: A setup guide the first time you open IPAForge, and a tour of every page.

install.title: Install and preload
install.body: One-click SideStore, app sources, the Apps page, Repair SideStore, QR codes, the checklist.

desktop.title: Desktop app
desktop.body: Installers for Windows, macOS and Linux, signed releases, and automatic updates.

management.title: Management tools
management.body: The Developer Portal page: your team's certificates and the apps each one signs, App IDs, profiles, app groups and devices. Pairing files per app, in one place.

wireless.title: Wireless and remote pairing
wireless.body: The iOS 17.4+ remote pairing file for SideStore, Wi-Fi without usbmuxd, the iOS 17.4+ device tunnel, and Apple TV and Vision Pro paired by their code. Next: installing to Apple TV and Vision Pro.

release.body: Windows code signing and Apple notarisation, more languages, a security review, and the signer on npm.

final.title: Get IPAForge.
final.sub: Free for Windows, macOS and Linux. It keeps itself up to date.

install-home.caption: Pick SideStore, or LiveContainer with SideStore, and see what the install will use before anything changes: App IDs left this week, free-app slots, the certificate and the team.

preload.caption: Add apps from the catalog, from sources, from a link or from .ipa files. Each one is checked against your iPhone first, then they install in one run.

apps.alt: The Apps page listing installed apps with when each one expires.
apps.caption: Every app you sideloaded and when it expires. Refresh, update or remove it, or let IPAForge refresh it by itself before it expires.

developer.alt: The Developer Portal page: the team's certificates, with who made each and which apps on the iPhone it signs.
developer.caption: See what your Apple ID holds at Apple: certificates and the apps each one signs, App IDs and how many are left this week, the profiles on your iPhone, app groups and registered devices. Clean up what nothing uses.

repair.alt: Repair SideStore checking SideStore line by line.
repair.caption: Repair SideStore checks who signed it, its certificate, its pairing file and when it expires, then fixes what keeps it from refreshing by itself.

devices.alt: The Devices page with the checklist for an iPhone.
devices.caption: A checklist for each device, for its iOS version: what IPAForge sees ticks itself, what only you can see on the iPhone has a box to tick.

sidestore-qr.alt: A QR code that adds a source to SideStore.
sidestore-qr.caption: Scan a code with your iPhone to add a source to SideStore, or to have SideStore install an app itself.

faq.title: IPAForge FAQ: cost, requirements, Apple ID and updates
faq.description: Short answers about IPAForge: what it costs, what you need, the warnings on first open, your password, updates and getting help.
faq.intro: Short answers, each pointing to the page with the details.

items.a: Yes. IPAForge is free and open source under the GNU AGPL-3.0, and a free Apple ID is enough to use it. Every feature is free for everyone; if it saves you time, you can support it on Patreon.

items.q: Do I need a paid Apple developer account?
items.a: No. A free Apple ID works, within Apple's limits: 3 sideloaded apps at a time on each device, 7 days per signature and 10 App IDs a week. IPAForge shows each before it changes anything, and refreshes your apps before they expire. A paid account works too, without those limits.

items.q: Why does macOS or Windows warn me when I open it?
items.a: IPAForge isn't notarised by Apple or code-signed for Windows yet. Install shows the one-time steps for each system. Both come with 1.0.

items.q: What do I need on Windows and Linux?
items.a: On Windows, install Apple Devices from the Microsoft Store, so your computer can talk to the iPhone. On Linux, install usbmuxd. macOS needs nothing extra.
iOS 15 or later with a passcode. On iOS 16 and later, Developer Mode must be on; the checklist on the Devices page shows how.

items.q: Where does my Apple ID password go?
items.a: Only to Apple. If you choose to save it, it stays encrypted in your system keychain on your computer.

Yes. It checks for a new version when it opens, and installs it only after its release signature checks out. Copies installed from a .msi, .deb or .rpm say when a new version is out, and which file to download. Release notes list every version.
Every error has a code and its fix right in the app. Troubleshooting lists every code. Still stuck? Ask on Discord, or open an issue on GitHub with the logs attached (Logs › Save in the app).
No. IPAForge is an independent project that installs SideStore and works alongside it. It isn't affiliated with SideStore or Apple.
